## 1.

Rank the validation set approach, k-fold CV with k = 5 or 10, and LOOCV from most to least biased as an estimate of test error. Then rank them again from most to least variable.

a. Justify the bias ranking in terms of how many observations each procedure trains on.
b. Justify the variance ranking in terms of how similar the training sets are across folds or splits, and how correlated the resulting error estimates are with each other.
c. A classmate argues that LOOCV averages n numbers, so by the law of large numbers it must have the lowest variance of the three. What is wrong with this argument?
d. Describe a situation where you would choose the validation set approach anyway, despite its higher bias.

## 5.

For each scenario, name the cross-validation strategy from lecture that
fits, from `KFold`, `StratifiedKFold`, `GroupKFold`, or a split that
respects time order. Explain in one or two sentences what would go wrong
with plain `KFold` instead.

a. Predicting whether a patient has a rare condition present in 2% of cases, from lab values measured once per patient.
b. Predicting a student's final exam score from their homework scores, where each of 40 students contributes eight weekly homework rows.
c. Predicting tomorrow's closing price from the last 30 days of prices, when the model will only ever be used on days after the ones it was trained on.
d. Predicting a customer's credit default from balance and income, one row per customer, with a 3% default rate.
